claim: Von Willebrand factor is produced in vascular endothelial cells and packaged into specialized secretory granules called Weibel-Palade bodies at the trans-Golgi network.
source: The hemostatic protein von Willebrand factor is produced in vascular endothelial cells and packaged into specialized secretory granules, Weibel–Palade bodies (WPBs) at the trans-Golgi network (TGN).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing the biological context of VWF and WPBs.

claim: V0a1, a V-ATPase component, is required for the membrane fission of Weibel-Palade bodies.
source: Here, we reported that V0a1, a V-ATPase component, is required for the membrane fission of WPBs.
evidence: This is the main finding reported in the abstract, supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Two V0a isoforms, V0a1 and V0a2, are found in distinct populations of WPBs in cultured endothelial cells.
source: We identified two V0a isoforms in distinct populations of WPBs in cultured endothelial cells, V0a1 and V0a2, on mature and nascent WPBs, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data showing differential localization of V0a1 and V0a2.

claim: V0a1 is localized on mature WPBs.
source: We identified two V0a isoforms in distinct populations of WPBs in cultured endothelial cells, V0a1 and V0a2, on mature and nascent WPBs, respectively.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence showing V0a1 on peripheral WPBs and colocalization with Rab27a, a mature WPB marker.

claim: V0a2 is localized on nascent WPBs.
source: We identified two V0a isoforms in distinct populations of WPBs in cultured endothelial cells, V0a1 and V0a2, on mature and nascent WPBs, respectively.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence and live cell imaging showing V0a2 on perinuclear WPB buds at the TGN.

claim: WPB buds are formed but cannot separate from the TGN in the absence of V0a1.
source: Although WPB buds were formed, WPBs could not separate from the TGN in the absence of V0a1.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data showing perinuclear accumulation of WPBs in V0a1-depleted cells.

claim: Protein kinase D (PKD) is an essential factor in biogenesis of WPBs.
source: Screening using dominant–negative forms of known membrane fission regulators revealed protein kinase D (PKD) as an essential factor in biogenesis of WPBs.
evidence: Supported by data showing that dominant-negative PKD mutants block WPB formation and trap VWF in tubules.

claim: Induction of wild-type PKDs in V0a1-depleted cells does not support the segregation of WPBs from the TGN.
source: Further, we showed that the induction of wild-type PKDs in V0a1-depleted cells does not support the segregation of WPBs from the TGN; suggesting a primary role of V0a1 in the membrane fission of WPBs.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data showing accumulation of wild-type PKDs on perinuclear WPBs in V0a1-depleted cells without rescue of WPB segregation.

claim: V0a1 has a primary role in the membrane fission of WPBs.
source: Further, we showed that the induction of wild-type PKDs in V0a1-depleted cells does not support the segregation of WPBs from the TGN; suggesting a primary role of V0a1 in the membrane fission of WPBs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that PKD overexpression cannot rescue the V0a1 depletion phenotype.

claim: Approximately one-third of newly synthesized proteins transition from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi apparatus.
source: Approximately one-third of newly synthesized proteins, including secretory proteins, transition from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi apparatus, thereby allowing versatile protein modifications, such as disulfide bond formation (Chen et al., 2005; Farquhar and Palade, 1981; Klumperman, 2011).
evidence: This is a general statement about protein trafficking supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Proteins reach the trans-Golgi network after transitioning through the Golgi apparatus.
source: Subsequently, the proteins reach the membrane compartment, called the trans-Golgi network (TGN) (Klumperman, 2011).
evidence: This is a general statement about protein trafficking supported by a citation.

claim: At the TGN, proteins are sorted and packaged as cargos into distinct transport carriers.
source: At the TGN, the proteins are sorted and packaged as cargos into distinct transport carriers that are targeted to individual subcellular destinations, such as the plasma membrane, endosomes, and/or secretory granules in specialized cells (De Matteis and Luini, 2008; Kienzle and von Blume, 2014; Pakdel and von Blume, 2018; Anitei and Hoflack, 2011).
evidence: This is a general statement about TGN function supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Biogenesis of membrane-bound structures is initiated by the deformation of the TGN membrane to form a bud where cargo proteins are packaged.
source: Biogenesis of such membrane-bound structures is initiated by the deformation of the TGN membrane, which functions as a donor membrane, to form a bud where cargo proteins are packaged.
evidence: This is a general statement about membrane trafficking supported by established knowledge.

claim: Formation of nascent buds is sometimes associated with the recruitment of coat proteins, clathrin, and coat protein I.
source: The formation of nascent buds is sometimes associated with the recruitment of the coat proteins, clathrin, and coat protein I (Kümmel and Reinisch, 2011; Antonny, 2006).
evidence: This is a general statement about bud formation supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Membrane fission is the process of division of one membrane into two.
source: The process of division of one membrane into two is termed membrane fission, which is expected to occur in leak-free luminal contents (Campelo and Malhotra, 2012; Renard et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a definition supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The difficulty in segregating the membrane fission process from other steps of biogenesis is due to the small size of membrane-bound structures formed at the TGN.
source: One plausible reason is the difficulty in segregating the membrane fission process from the other steps of biogenesis in cells due to the small membrane-bound structures, such as secretory vesicles that are 50–100 nm in diameter, formed at the TGN (Campelo and Malhotra, 2012; Renard et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for why membrane fission is poorly understood, supported by citations.

claim: Von Willebrand factor is an extra-large multimeric glycoprotein involved in primary hemostasis by adhering platelets to sites of vascular injury.
source: The von Willebrand factor (VWF) is an extra-large multimeric glycoprotein involved in primary hemostasis by adhering platelets to the sites of vascular injury (Sadler, 2005; Sadler, 1998; Wagner, 1990).
evidence: This is a general statement about VWF function supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: VWF multimers found in plasma vary in size, with the largest multimer having a molecular mass of 20 MDa.
source: The multimers found in plasma vary in size; the largest multimer has a molecular mass of 20 MDa (Fowler et al., 1985; Zheng, 2015).
evidence: This is a factual statement about VWF multimer size supported by citations.

claim: Larger VWF multimers recruit platelets more efficiently.
source: Larger multimers recruit platelets more efficiently; thus, the multimerization of VWF is crucial for hemostasis (Federici et al., 1989).
evidence: This is a statement about VWF function supported by a citation.

claim: VWF is synthesized in vascular endothelial cells as a single polypeptide with a molecular mass of 350 kDa in the endoplasmic reticulum.
source: VWF is synthesized in vascular endothelial cells as a single polypeptide with a molecular mass of 350 kDa in the endoplasmic reticulum and immediately forms a disulfide bond-dependent dimer.
evidence: This is a statement about VWF biosynthesis supported by established knowledge.

claim: VWF dimers are transported through the Golgi apparatus where they convert to multimers via disulfide bond formation.
source: The dimers are then transported through the Golgi apparatus, where they convert dimers to multimers via disulfide bond formation.
evidence: This is a statement about VWF biosynthesis supported by established knowledge.

claim: VWF multimers are stored in large secretory granules called Weibel-Palade bodies.
source: The multimers are stored in large secretory granules called Weibel–Palade bodies (WPBs) (McCormack et al., 2017; Metcalf et al., 2008; Mourik and Eikenboom, 2017; Valentijn et al., 2011; Weibel, 2012).
evidence: This is a statement about VWF storage supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: WPBs are endothelial cell-specific, elongated, rod-shaped secretory organelles varying in size from 0.5 to 5 μm.
source: WPBs are endothelial cell-specific, elongated, rod-shaped secretory organelles varying in size from 0.5 to 5 μm.
evidence: This is a descriptive statement about WPB morphology supported by established knowledge.

claim: VWF multimers in WPBs are exocytosed in response to several stimulants, such as histamine.
source: VWF multimers in WPBs are exocytosed in response to several stimulants, such as histamine.
evidence: This is a statement about WPB function supported by established knowledge and experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: In electron tomography, VWF multimers in the WPB lumen are found as striated, paracrystalline matrices called VWF tubules.
source: In electron tomography, VWF multimers in the WPB lumen are found as striated, paracrystalline matrices called VWF tubules (Berriman et al., 2009; Valentijn et al., 2008; Zenner et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a statement about VWF structure in WPBs supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: VWF tubules are aligned in parallel along the longitudinal axes of WPBs.
source: As VWF tubules are aligned in parallel along the longitudinal axes of WPBs, it is thought that the formation of VWF tubules drives the formation of the unique, elongated shape of the organelles.
evidence: This is a statement about VWF tubule organization supported by established knowledge.

claim: The formation of VWF tubules drives the formation of the unique, elongated shape of WPBs.
source: As VWF tubules are aligned in parallel along the longitudinal axes of WPBs, it is thought that the formation of VWF tubules drives the formation of the unique, elongated shape of the organelles.
evidence: This is an inference about the relationship between VWF tubule formation and WPB shape.

claim: VWF tubule formation is a highly coordinated process of the alignment of multiple VWF dimers into a right-handed coil and the conversion of the aligned dimers into large multimers.
source: In vitro reconstitution studies suggest that VWF tubule formation is a highly coordinated process of the alignment of multiple VWF dimers into a right-handed coil and the conversion of the aligned dimers into large multimers (McCormack et al., 2017; Huang et al., 2008; Mayadas and Wagner, 1989; Zhou et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a statement about VWF tubule formation supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: VWF tubulation allows approximately 50-fold compaction of VWF in WPBs.
source: This tubulation allows approximately 50-fold compaction of the VWF in WPBs.
evidence: This is a statement about VWF compaction supported by established knowledge.

claim: VWF tubulation requires acidic pH and Ca2+ in vitro.
source: The tubulation process requires acidic pH and Ca2+ in vitro (Huang et al., 2008; Zhou et al., 2011; Gerke, 2011; Springer, 2011)
evidence: This is a statement about the requirements for VWF tubulation supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: VWF is expected to be exposed to acidic pH and Ca2+ during maturation, presumably at the TGN and/or in newly forming WPB buds from the TGN.
source: thus, VWF is expected to be exposed in such a subcellular environment during maturation, presumably at the TGN and/or in the newly forming WPB buds from the TGN (Gerke, 2011; Springer, 2011; Wagner et al., 1986).
evidence: This is an inference about where VWF tubulation occurs based on in vitro requirements and citations.

claim: The acidic milieu in mature WPBs is biologically significant.
source: The biological significance of the acidic milieu in mature WPBs is also evident.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that neutralization of WPBs impairs VWF function.

claim: Forced neutralization of the WPB lumen by chemical treatment causes a loss of visible VWF tubules, resulting in rounding of WPBs.
source: Forced neutralization of the WPB lumen by a chemical treatment causes a loss of visible VWF tubules, resulting in rounding of WPBs (Michaux et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a statement about the effect of neutralization on WPB structure supported by a citation.

claim: Neutralization of WPBs does not reduce agonist-evoked VWF exocytosis.
source: Neutralization does not reduce agonist-evoked VWF exocytosis; instead, it markedly reduces platelet recruitment because the multimers are unable to disperse efficiently upon exposure to an extracellular neutral environment.
evidence: This is a statement about the effect of neutralization on VWF function supported by a citation and experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: Neutralization of WPBs markedly reduces platelet recruitment because VWF multimers are unable to disperse efficiently upon exposure to an extracellular neutral environment.
source: Neutralization does not reduce agonist-evoked VWF exocytosis; instead, it markedly reduces platelet recruitment because the multimers are unable to disperse efficiently upon exposure to an extracellular neutral environment.
evidence: This is a statement about the effect of neutralization on VWF function supported by a citation and experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: The subcellular acidic milieu is biologically important for primary hemostasis mediated by VWF.
source: Thus, this evidence indicates the biological importance of the subcellular acidic milieu in primary hemostasis mediated by VWF; nevertheless, the mechanism by which endothelial cells achieve such an environment has not yet been addressed.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the effects of neutralization on VWF function.

claim: The mechanism by which endothelial cells achieve an acidic environment in WPBs has not yet been addressed.
source: Thus, this evidence indicates the biological importance of the subcellular acidic milieu in primary hemostasis mediated by VWF; nevertheless, the mechanism by which endothelial cells achieve such an environment has not yet been addressed.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge.

claim: V-ATPase is an ATP-driven proton pump.
source: Vacuolar H+-ATPase (V-ATPase), an ATP-driven proton pump, is a major regulator of the subcellular acidic pH in cells (Collins and Forgac, 2020; Maxson and Grinstein, 2014; Nakanishi-Matsui et al., 2010; Vasanthakumar and Rubinstein, 2020).
evidence: This is a general statement about V-ATPase function supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: V-ATPase is a major regulator of the subcellular acidic pH in cells.
source: Vacuolar H+-ATPase (V-ATPase), an ATP-driven proton pump, is a major regulator of the subcellular acidic pH in cells (Collins and Forgac, 2020; Maxson and Grinstein, 2014; Nakanishi-Matsui et al., 2010; Vasanthakumar and Rubinstein, 2020).
evidence: This is a general statement about V-ATPase function supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: V-ATPase is a multi-subunit complex composed of two large domains, V0 and V1.
source: It is a multi-subunit complex composed of two large domains, V0 and V1.
evidence: This is a general statement about V-ATPase structure supported by established knowledge.

claim: V0 is a membrane-embedded domain that translocates protons across the membrane.
source: V0 is a membrane-embedded domain that translocates protons across the membrane, whereas the V1 domain hydrolyzes ATP.
evidence: This is a general statement about V-ATPase structure and function supported by established knowledge.

claim: The V1 domain hydrolyzes ATP.
source: V0 is a membrane-embedded domain that translocates protons across the membrane, whereas the V1 domain hydrolyzes ATP.
evidence: This is a general statement about V-ATPase structure and function supported by established knowledge.

claim: In mammalian cells, several V-ATPase subunits exist in multiple isoforms encoded by distinct genes.
source: In mammalian cells, several subunits exist in multiple isoforms encoded by distinct genes, suggesting a large structural diversity of the V-ATPase complex in cells.
evidence: This is a general statement about V-ATPase diversity supported by established knowledge.

claim: The existence of multiple V-ATPase isoforms suggests a large structural diversity of the V-ATPase complex in cells.
source: In mammalian cells, several subunits exist in multiple isoforms encoded by distinct genes, suggesting a large structural diversity of the V-ATPase complex in cells.
evidence: This is an inference about V-ATPase diversity based on the existence of multiple isoforms.

claim: Not all cultured endothelial cells express VWF, particularly when cells are maintained in sparse conditions.
source: Although VWF is the most commonly used vascular endothelial cell marker in vivo (Wagner, 1990), not all cultured endothelial cells express VWF, particularly when cells are maintained in rather sparse conditions.
evidence: This is a statement about cell culture conditions supported by a citation and experimental observation.

claim: Primary cultured HUVECs form a stable monolayer with a characteristic cobblestone-like appearance when maintained on fibronectin for 5-6 days.
source: Primary cultured human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) form a stable monolayer with a characteristic cobblestone-like appearance when cells are maintained on fibronectin for 5–6 days.
evidence: This is a statement about cell culture conditions supported by experimental observation.

claim: Under optimized culture conditions, essentially all HUVECs expressed VWF at a comparable level.
source: Under these conditions, essentially all cells expressed VWF at a comparable level, and the cellular junction proteins were located along the cell boundary, as expected in differentiated endothelial cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Lipofection- and electroporation-based transfection considerably disturbed the cellular junction in HUVECs.
source: Although our tested lipofection- and electroporation-based transfection considerably disturbed the cellular junction, recombinant lentivirus-mediated expression of EGFP showed virtually no effect (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Recombinant lentivirus-mediated expression of EGFP showed virtually no effect on cellular junctions in HUVECs.
source: Although our tested lipofection- and electroporation-based transfection considerably disturbed the cellular junction, recombinant lentivirus-mediated expression of EGFP showed virtually no effect (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Four hours of exposure to V-ATPase inhibitors caused rounding of WPBs without affecting the secreted amount of VWF.
source: Four hours of exposure to the inhibitors caused rounding of WPBs without affecting the secreted amount of VWF (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B), as previously observed in chemically neutralized cells (Michaux et al., 2006), suggesting the possible role of V-ATPase in WPBs.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: Prolonged exposure to bafilomycin A1 (16 h) is reported to reduce the basal/constitutive secretion of VWF.
source: Note that prolonged exposure to bafilomycin A1 (16 h) is reported to reduce the basal/constitutive secretion of VWF (Torisu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a statement about the effect of prolonged V-ATPase inhibition supported by a citation.

claim: Pretreatment with V-ATPase inhibitors did not alter the regulated exocytosis induced by histamine.
source: While pretreatment with the V-ATPase inhibitors did not alter the regulated exocytosis induced by histamine (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D), it impaired the dispersion of VWF multimers, as observed in the cells exposed to NH4Cl, which neutralizes subcellular acidic compartments.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Pretreatment with V-ATPase inhibitors impaired the dispersion of VWF multimers.
source: While pretreatment with the V-ATPase inhibitors did not alter the regulated exocytosis induced by histamine (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D), it impaired the dispersion of VWF multimers, as observed in the cells exposed to NH4Cl, which neutralizes subcellular acidic compartments.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: The strings formed by tangled VWF multimers upon histamine exposure of V-ATPase inhibitor- or NH4Cl-pretreated cells were thin and fragile compared to those in non-pretreated cells.
source: The strings formed by tangled VWF multimers upon histamine exposure of the V-ATPase inhibitor- or NH4Cl-pretreated cells were rather thin and fragile compared to the prominent, thick structures observed in the non-pretreated cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: V-ATPase activity contributes to the acidic milieu inside WPBs.
source: These observations suggest the contribution of V-ATPase activity in the acidic milieu inside WPBs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the effects of V-ATPase inhibitors on WPB morphology and VWF multimer dispersion.

claim: V0c and V1A, two common subunits of the mammalian V-ATPase complex, are localized in WPBs in HUVECs.
source: Indeed, we confirmed the WPB localization of V0c and V1A, two common subunits of the mammalian V-ATPase complex, in HUVECs (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B.

claim: Endogenous V0a1 was mainly found in WPBs.
source: As observed in the EGFP-tagged V0a1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A), the endogenous V0a1 (isoform 1 of the V0a subunit) was mainly found in WPBs (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 4A.

claim: V0a1 signal was evident on WPBs observed in the cell periphery, whereas virtually no signal was observed on WPBs in the perinucleus.
source: The signal was evident on the WPBs observed in the cell periphery, whereas virtually no signal was observed on the WPBs in the perinucleus (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: WPBs are formed at the TGN and transported to the cell periphery upon maturation.
source: WPBs are formed at the TGN and transported to the cell periphery upon maturation, suggesting V0a1 localization in mature WPBs.
evidence: This is a statement about WPB trafficking supported by established knowledge.

claim: Rab27a is a well-characterized molecule recruited to WPBs during maturation.
source: Rab27a, a small GTPase, is a well-characterized molecule recruited to WPBs during maturation (Bierings et al., 2012; Nightingale et al., 2009; Rojo Pulido et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a statement about Rab27a function supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Post-budded WPBs from the TGN move along microtubules to the cell periphery, where they are anchored to actin fibers.
source: Post-budded WPBs from the TGN move along microtubules to the cell periphery, where they are anchored to actin fibers.
evidence: This is a statement about WPB trafficking supported by established knowledge.

claim: Rab27a is required for anchoring WPBs to actin.
source: Rab27a is required for anchoring WPBs to actin.
evidence: This is a statement about Rab27a function supported by established knowledge.

claim: V0a1 colocalized well with EGFP-Rab27a.
source: We found well-matched colocalization of V0a1 and EGFP-Rab27a (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: V0a1 is localized in mature WPBs in HUVECs.
source: Thus, V0a1 appears to be localized in mature WPBs in HUVECs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the colocalization of V0a1 with Rab27a and its peripheral localization.

claim: V0a2-EGFP was localized only on the perinuclear WPBs but not on the peripheral WPBs.
source: V0a2 showed the opposite localization to V0a1; V0a2-EGFP was localized only on the perinuclear WPBs but not on the peripheral WPBs (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Endogenous V0a2 protein was detected in the buds emerging from the TGN as well as on the TGN.
source: Accordingly, endogenous V0a2 protein was detected in the buds emerging from the TGN as well as on the TGN (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4B.

claim: V0a2-EGFP is located on the perinuclear WPB buds but not often found in post-budded WPBs.
source: Super resolution microscopy revealed that V0a2-EGFP is located on the perinuclear WPB buds; however, they are not often found in post-budded WPBs (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The signal intensity of VWF found in the V0a2-positive WPBs was faint compared to the strong signal observed in the post-budded WPBs.
source: The signal intensity of VWF found in the V0a2-positive WPBs was rather faint compared to the strong signal observed in the post-budded WPBs (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: V0a2-EGFP was considerably localized in the newly forming bud and disappeared as soon as the bud segregated from the Golgi apparatus.
source: Live cell imaging confirmed that V0a2-EGFP was considerably localized in the newly forming bud and disappeared as soon as the bud segregated from the Golgi apparatus (Figure 2C and Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 2C and Video 1.

claim: V0a2 buds found around the TGN were completely absent from EGFP-Rab27a.
source: The V0a2 buds found around the TGN were completely absent from EGFP-Rab27a, a mature WPB marker (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: V0a2 is localized in nascent WPBs.
source: These observations indicated the limited localization of V0a2 in nascent WPBs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the localization of V0a2 on perinuclear WPB buds and its absence from mature WPBs.

claim: Newly forming WPB buds in the TGN are clathrin-coated.
source: Newly forming WPB buds in the TGN are clathrin-coated Zenner et al., 2007.
evidence: This is a statement about WPB bud structure supported by a citation.

claim: Depletion of the Golgi-associated clathrin adaptor protein-1 (AP-1) results in an almost total loss of visible WPBs.
source: Depletion of the Golgi-associated clathrin adaptor protein-1 (AP-1) results in an almost total loss of visible WPBs Lui-Roberts et al., 2005.
evidence: This is a statement about the role of AP-1 in WPB biogenesis supported by a citation.

claim: Clathrin is an essential factor for biogenesis of WPBs, presumably required for a very early step, such as the bud-forming process at the TGN.
source: Thus, clathrin appears to be an essential factor for biogenesis of WPBs, presumably required for a very early step, such as the bud-forming process at the TGN.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the effects of AP-1 depletion on WPB formation.

claim: Nascent WPBs found in the perinucleus were partially decorated with the components of AP-1 complex.
source: Corroborating the findings of earlier studies, nascent WPBs found in the perinucleus were partially decorated with the components of AP-1 complex (Figure 1—figure supplement 5A,B); however, this was not as evident as observed in V0a2-EGFP (Figure 2A–B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5A,B.

claim: V0a1 and V0a2 are the predominant V0a isoforms located on WPBs in HUVECs.
source: As the two other V0a isoforms did not show evident WPB localization as observed in V0a1 and V0a2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 6A,B), we concluded that V0a1 and V0a2 are the predominant V0a isoforms located on WPBs in HUVECs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that V0a3 and V0a4 do not show evident WPB localization.

claim: V-ATPase blockage caused a selective induction of dimer secretion.
source: While V-ATPase blockage did not change the amount of basally/constitutively secreted VWF (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B), the multimer analysis revealed that it caused a selective induction of dimer secretion (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), suggesting a requirement for cellular V-ATPase activity in multimerization.
evidence: This is supported by VWF multimer analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Cellular V-ATPase activity is required for VWF multimerization.
source: While V-ATPase blockage did not change the amount of basally/constitutively secreted VWF (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B), the multimer analysis revealed that it caused a selective induction of dimer secretion (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), suggesting a requirement for cellular V-ATPase activity in multimerization.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that V-ATPase inhibition causes dimer secretion.

claim: The dimer secretion caused by V-ATPase blockage occurs from the TGN via the constitutive secretion pathway.
source: As the dimer secretion is blocked by brefeldin A, an ER-to-Golgi transport inhibitor (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), it is likely that the dimer secretion caused by V-ATPase blockage occurs from the TGN via the constitutive secretion pathway.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that brefeldin A blocks dimer secretion induced by V-ATPase inhibition.

claim: V-ATPase inhibitor exposure caused a rapid disappearance of the nascent WPB buds.
source: The V-ATPase inhibitor exposure also caused a rapid disappearance of the nascent WPB buds (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, compared with Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: VWF multimerization occurring at the TGN and/or in nascent WPB buds requires V-ATPase activity.
source: The above observations suggested that VWF multimerization occurring at the TGN and/or in nascent WPB buds require V-ATPase activity.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the effects of V-ATPase inhibition on dimer secretion and nascent WPB bud formation.

claim: Depletion of either V0a1 or V0a2 caused an increase in the secreted amount of VWF multimers.
source: Although the depletion of either V0a1 or V0a2 caused an increase in the secreted amount of VWF multimers, unexpectedly, no detectable alteration was observed in the multimer status even when both isoforms were depleted (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by VWF multimer analysis data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: No detectable alteration was observed in the VWF multimer status when both V0a1 and V0a2 were depleted.
source: Although the depletion of either V0a1 or V0a2 caused an increase in the secreted amount of VWF multimers, unexpectedly, no detectable alteration was observed in the multimer status even when both isoforms were depleted (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by VWF multimer analysis data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Bafilomycin A1 and concanamycin A exposure caused almost complete neutralization of the TGN.
source: Bafilomycin A1 and concanamycin A exposure caused almost complete neutralization of the TGN, whereas the depletion of each V0a isoform resulted in a modest increase of the pH (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by pH measurement data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Depletion of each V0a isoform resulted in a modest increase of the TGN pH.
source: Bafilomycin A1 and concanamycin A exposure caused almost complete neutralization of the TGN, whereas the depletion of each V0a isoform resulted in a modest increase of the pH (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by pH measurement data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The luminal acidic environment of the TGN is largely maintained by V-ATPase activity in HUVECs.
source: These observations suggest that the luminal acidic environment of the TGN is largely maintained by V-ATPase activity in HUVECs, but the contribution of V0a1 and V0a2 is limited or masked by functional redundancies.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the effects of V-ATPase inhibition and V0a isoform depletion on TGN pH.

claim: The contribution of V0a1 and V0a2 to TGN acidification is limited or masked by functional redundancies.
source: These observations suggest that the luminal acidic environment of the TGN is largely maintained by V-ATPase activity in HUVECs, but the contribution of V0a1 and V0a2 is limited or masked by functional redundancies.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the modest effects of V0a isoform depletion on TGN pH.

claim: V0a2 depletion resulted in a slight but homogenous increase of the luminal TGN pH.
source: Consistent with the nascent WPB/TGN localization, V0a2 depletion resulted in a slight but homogenous increase of the luminal TGN pH (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by pH measurement data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: V0a1 depletion caused relatively large pH increase only in some TGN subdomains.
source: In contrast, although no statistical difference was observed when the whole TGN pH was compared (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A), V0a1 depletion caused relatively large pH increase only in the some TGN subdomains (arrowheads in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B); suggesting an involvement of V0a1 in the pH regulation of the TGN, although the main cellular pool is found on peripheral WPBs.
evidence: This is supported by pH measurement data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: V0a1 is involved in the pH regulation of the TGN.
source: In contrast, although no statistical difference was observed when the whole TGN pH was compared (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A), V0a1 depletion caused relatively large pH increase only in the some TGN subdomains (arrowheads in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B); suggesting an involvement of V0a1 in the pH regulation of the TGN, although the main cellular pool is found on peripheral WPBs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that V0a1 depletion causes pH increase in some TGN subdomains.

claim: V0a1 and V0a2 appear to be dispensable for multimer formation.
source: Taken together, despite the considerable localization on WPBs as well as the partial contribution on the acidic microenvironment of the TGN, V0a1 and V0a2 appear to be dispensable for multimer formation; however, the roles of these V0a isoforms remain elusive.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that V0a isoform depletion does not affect VWF multimer status.

claim: An increase in basal/constitutive VWF secretion is often observed in cells showing an alteration in biogenesis of WPBs.
source: An increase in basal/constitutive VWF secretion is often observed in cells showing an alteration in biogenesis of WPBs (Nightingale et al., 2009; Lui-Roberts et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a statement about the relationship between WPB biogenesis and VWF secretion supported by citations.

claim: Depletion of V0a2 resulted in the formation of irregular, twisted WPBs.
source: Depletion of V0a2, which is found in the nascent WPBs, resulted in the formation of irregular, twisted WPBs compared to those found in the control (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Feret's diameters of WPBs, particularly Fmax/Fmin in the V0a2-depleted cells were smaller than those in the control.
source: Accordingly, Feret's diameters of WPBs, particularly Fmax/Fmin in the V0a2-depleted cells were obviously smaller than those in the control (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of WPB morphology shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The phenotype of irregular WPBs in V0a2-depleted cells was specifically rescued by shRNA-resistant V0a2 expression.
source: To confirm the shRNA-mediated phenotype, we introduced HA-tagged shRNA-resistant V0a2 in shRNA-expressing cells. The phenotype was specifically rescued in the resistant V0a2 expressing cells; however, this was not observed in the non-transfected cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The number of WPBs formed in the V0a2-depleted cells was comparable to that in the control.
source: The number of WPBs formed in the V0a2-depleted cells was comparable to that in the control (Figure 4B), suggesting that V0a2 is not essential for the separation of WPBs from the TGN at the site of biogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of WPB number shown in Figure 4B.

claim: V0a2 is not essential for the separation of WPBs from the TGN at the site of biogenesis.
source: The number of WPBs formed in the V0a2-depleted cells was comparable to that in the control (Figure 4B), suggesting that V0a2 is not essential for the separation of WPBs from the TGN at the site of biogenesis.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that V0a2 depletion does not reduce WPB number.

claim: VWFD1-A1-HA was found in irregularly shaped WPBs located away from the TGN in V0a2-depleted cells.
source: To further confirm the significance of V0a2 in biogenesis of WPBs, HUVECs were transduced with recombinant lentiviral particles expressing HA-tagged VWF after confirmed the depletion of endogenous V0a2 protein (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C). VWFD1-A1-HA was found in the irregularly shaped WPBs located away from the TGN (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: WPBs in V0a2-depleted cells were decorated with EGFP-Rab27a.
source: The WPBs were decorated with EGFP-Rab27a (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The membrane-bound structure of WPBs can still be formed and transported to the cell periphery in the absence of V0a2.
source: These observations indicate that the membrane-bound structure of WPBs can still be formed and transported to the cell periphery, even in the absence of V0a2, although it appears to be important for the formation of properly shaped WPBs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that WPBs in V0a2-depleted cells are decorated with Rab27a and located away from the TGN.

claim: V0a2 is important for the formation of properly shaped WPBs.
source: These observations indicate that the membrane-bound structure of WPBs can still be formed and transported to the cell periphery, even in the absence of V0a2, although it appears to be important for the formation of properly shaped WPBs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that V0a2 depletion results in irregular WPB morphology.

claim: V0a1 depletion caused the perinuclear accumulation of WPBs.
source: The phenotype induced by the depletion of V0a1, which is found in the peripheral mature WPBs, is more striking. The number of WPBs in the V0a1-depleted cells was substantially decreased compared to that in the control, and the formed WPBs were largely accumulated around the TGN (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The number of WPBs in the V0a1-depleted cells was substantially decreased compared to that in the control.
source: The phenotype induced by the depletion of V0a1, which is found in the peripheral mature WPBs, is more striking. The number of WPBs in the V0a1-depleted cells was substantially decreased compared to that in the control, and the formed WPBs were largely accumulated around the TGN (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of WPB number shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The perinuclear accumulation of WPBs in V0a1-depleted cells was rescued by the induction of shRNA-resistant V0a1.
source: The perinuclear accumulation of WPBs was rescued by the induction of shRNA-resistant V0a1 (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: VWFD1-A1 and P-selectin were trapped in the perinuclear buds originating from the TGN in the absence of V0a1.
source: The phenotype was further confirmed by the induction of tagged VWFD1-A1 and P-selectin in V0a1-depleted cells (Figure 4D–E). P-selectin is a leukocyte-recruiting protein that is packaged into WPBs at the TGN (Harrison-Lavoie et al., 2006; Larsen et al., 1989). Both proteins were trapped in the perinuclear buds originating from the TGN in the absence of V0a1 (Figure 4D–E).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4D-E.

claim: The accumulated WPB buds in V0a1-depleted cells were not EGFP-Rab27a-positive.
source: The accumulated WPB buds were not EGFP-Rab27a-positive (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The accumulated WPBs in the V0a1-depleted cells were rather static compared to those in the control.
source: Live cell imaging showed that the accumulated WPBs in the V0a1-depleted cells were rather static compared to those in the control (Videos 2 and 3).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Videos 2 and 3.

claim: Newly forming WPBs cannot be separated from the TGN in the absence of V0a1.
source: These observations suggest that newly forming WPBs cannot be separated from the TGN in the absence of V0a1.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that WPBs accumulate around the TGN in V0a1-depleted cells.

claim: No apparent alteration of microtubule and actin networks was observed in the V0a1-depleted cells.
source: We believe that disruption of cytoskeletal architecture is unlikely because we were unable to observe any apparent alteration of microtubule and actin networks in the V0a1-depleted cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Induction of a dominant-negative form of dynactin 2 or myosin Va did not mimic the phenotype upon V0a1-depletion.
source: Accordingly, the induction of a dominant-negative form of either dynactin 2 (Rondaij et al., 2006) or myosin Va (Rojo Pulido et al., 2011), which disturbs the microtubule or actin network-mediating transport of WPBs, did not mimic the phenotype upon V0a1-depletion (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: Induction of kinase-dead mutants of PKD family members significantly impaired the formation of WPBs.
source: Although the dominant-negative forms of various splicing variants of dynamin 2, dynamin 3, and CtBP1/BARS are virtually ineffective in biogenesis of WPBs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, Figure 5—figure supplement 2), we found that the induction of the kinase-dead mutants of the PKD family members (PKD1K612N, PKD2K580N, and PKD3K605N) in HUVECs significantly impaired the formation of WPBs (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 3A,B,C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 3A,B,C.

claim: Endogenous VWF protein was found in the tubules formed by all three PKD mutants.
source: Endogenous VWF protein was found in the tubules formed by all three PKD mutants (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 3A,B), indicating that the membrane fission of WPBs at the TGN requires PKDs.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 3A,B.

claim: The membrane fission of WPBs at the TGN requires PKDs.
source: Endogenous VWF protein was found in the tubules formed by all three PKD mutants (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 3A,B), indicating that the membrane fission of WPBs at the TGN requires PKDs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that dominant-negative PKD mutants block WPB formation and trap VWF in tubules.

claim: EGFP-PKD1WT was found mainly in the cytosol and certain parts of the TGN in the control cells.
source: We further investigated whether V0a1 had any effect on the subcellular localization of wild-type PKDs (PKDsWT). EGFP-PKD1WT was found mainly in the cytosol and certain parts of the TGN in the control cells, as reported earlier (Figure 5B; Bard and Malhotra, 2006; Malhotra and Campelo, 2011; Van Lint et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: EGFP-PKDsWT substantially accumulated on the WPBs retained around the TGN upon V0a1 depletion.
source: In contrast, EGFP-PKDsWT substantially accumulated on the WPBs, which were retained around the TGN upon V0a1 depletion (Figure 5B–E, Figure 5—figure supplement 3D,E).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5B-E and Figure 5—figure supplement 3D,E.

claim: Induction of PKDsWT is not enough to induce the separation of WPBs from the TGN in the V0a1-depleted cells.
source: The induction of PKDsWT appears to be not enough to induce the separation of WPBs from the TGN in the V0a1-depleted cells.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that PKDsWT accumulate on WPBs in V0a1-depleted cells without rescuing WPB segregation.

claim: Endogenous PKD2 protein accumulated in the V0a1-depleted cells.
source: A similar accumulation of endogenous PKD2 protein was observed in the V0a1-depleted cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4.

claim: The segregation of newly forming WPB buds from the TGN is mediated by PKD-dependent membrane fission.
source: Thus, the above observations indicate that the segregation of newly forming WPB buds from the TGN is mediated by PKD-dependent membrane fission, and suggest that either V0a1 is required for this process or that V0a1 and PKD coordinate with each other in this process.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that dominant-negative PKD mutants block WPB formation.

claim: Either V0a1 is required for PKD-dependent membrane fission or V0a1 and PKD coordinate with each other in this process.
source: Thus, the above observations indicate that the segregation of newly forming WPB buds from the TGN is mediated by PKD-dependent membrane fission, and suggest that either V0a1 is required for this process or that V0a1 and PKD coordinate with each other in this process.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that PKD overexpression cannot rescue the V0a1 depletion phenotype.

claim: DAG was present on the membrane of newly forming WPBs.
source: These observations showed that DAG was present on the membrane of newly forming WPBs, and PKDs were recruited through the interaction with DAG.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data showing DAG reporters on perinuclear WPBs.

claim: PKDs were recruited to newly forming WPBs through the interaction with DAG.
source: These observations showed that DAG was present on the membrane of newly forming WPBs, and PKDs were recruited through the interaction with DAG.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the presence of DAG on WPBs and the known DAG-binding properties of PKDs.

claim: A large DAG pool was detected on the TGN.
source: A large DAG pool was detected on the TGN, as expected from an earlier study (Figure 6A; Lehel et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: EGFP-PKCε-C1 was found in the perinuclear WPB buds in the control group.
source: The reporter was also found in the perinuclear WPB buds in the control group (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: EGFP-PKCε-C1 signal was more evident in the accumulated WPB buds formed upon V0a1-depletion.
source: The signal was more evident in the accumulated WPB buds formed upon V0a1-depletion (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: PI4P was present on perinuclear newly forming WPBs.
source: Two additional PI4P reporters, PH-FAPP1-EGFP (Balla et al., 2005) and EGFP-P4M-SidM (Hammond et al., 2014), also showed similar results (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B,C), indicating a presence of PI4P on perinuclear newly forming WPBs.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data showing PI4P reporters on perinuclear WPBs.

claim: V0a1-depletion mediated by two independent shRNAs caused an increase of total PKD1 protein compared with the control.
source: V0a1-depletion mediated by two independent shRNAs caused an increase of total PKD1 protein compared with the control, whereas we were unable to see any detectable changes in the level of phosphorylated PKD1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: No detectable changes in the level of phosphorylated PKD1 were observed upon V0a1-depletion.
source: V0a1-depletion mediated by two independent shRNAs caused an increase of total PKD1 protein compared with the control, whereas we were unable to see any detectable changes in the level of phosphorylated PKD1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: V-ATPase has been suggested to regulate membrane fusion by generating electrochemical gradients or as a structural component of the fusion machinery.
source: V-ATPase has been suggested to regulate membrane fusion by generating electrochemical gradients or as a structural component of the fusion machinery (Merz, 2015), whereas any involvement in membrane fission has not been described previously.
evidence: This is a statement about previous knowledge of V-ATPase function supported by a citation.

claim: Any involvement of V-ATPase in membrane fission has not been described previously.
source: V-ATPase has been suggested to regulate membrane fusion by generating electrochemical gradients or as a structural component of the fusion machinery (Merz, 2015), whereas any involvement in membrane fission has not been described previously.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the findings.

claim: V0a1 and V0a2 were detected in WPB proteomes.
source: Consistent with our findings, these V0a isoforms were detected in WPB proteomes (Holthenrich et al., 2019; van Breevoort et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a statement about previous proteomic studies supported by citations.

claim: V0a2 is not essential for bud formation or membrane fission of WPBs despite the specific localization on newly forming WPBs.
source: V0a2 appears to be required for the formation of proper, elongated shaped WPBs, whereas it is not essential for bud formation or membrane fission of WPBs despite the specific localization on newly forming WPBs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that V0a2 depletion results in irregular WPB morphology but does not reduce WPB number.

claim: V0a1 is found on small intracellular vesicles in addition to WPBs.
source: V0a1 is also found on small intracellular vesicles in addition to WPBs; perhaps, these are acidic subcellular compartments such as endosomes and lysosomes.
evidence: This is an observation from the immunofluorescence data.

claim: Endosomes are observed to form close contacts with WPBs in electron tomographic analysis.
source: Endosomes are observed to form close contacts with WPBs in electron tomographic analysis (Berriman et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a statement about previous electron tomography studies supported by a citation.

claim: The endosomal/lysosomal tetraspanin CD63/LAMP3 is delivered to WPBs during maturation.
source: The endosomal/lysosomal tetraspanin CD63/LAMP3 is delivered to WPBs during maturation (Harrison-Lavoie et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a statement about WPB maturation supported by a citation.

claim: Small vesicle-mediated transfer of V0a1 could drive the membrane fission of nascent WPBs.
source: Thus, it is likely that the small vesicle-mediated transfer of V0a1 could drive the membrane fission of nascent WPBs.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for how V0a1 might function in membrane fission.

claim: The biogenesis of WPBs occurs at particular subdomains of the TGN.
source: Relatively large pH increase was observed in some TGN subdomains in the V0a1-depleted cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B) possibly suggests that the biogenesis of WPBs occurs at particular subdomains of the TGN.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that V0a1 depletion causes pH increase in some TGN subdomains.

claim: DAG accumulation on nascent WPBs became more evident in the absence of V0a1.
source: DAG accumulation on nascent WPBs became more evident in the absence of V0a1.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data showing increased DAG reporter signal on accumulated WPBs in V0a1-depleted cells.

claim: Insertion of the N-terminal hydrophobic stretch of PKDs into the outer leaflet of the TGN is suggested to assist membrane fission by generating membrane curvature.
source: Insertion of the N-terminal hydrophobic stretch of PKDs into the outer leaflet of the TGN is suggested to assist membrane fission by generating membrane curvature (Campelo and Malhotra, 2012; Malhotra and Campelo, 2011).
evidence: This is a statement about a proposed mechanism of PKD function supported by citations.

claim: The hydrophobic stretch-mediating mechanism is unlikely in the biogenesis of WPBs.
source: We believe that the hydrophobic stretch-mediating mechanism is unlikely in the biogenesis of WPBs because we observed essentially equivalent effects on all PKD members, including PKD3, which lacks the hydrophobic stretch in the structure (Campelo and Malhotra, 2012).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that all PKD members have similar effects on WPB biogenesis.

claim: There is functional redundancy of PKDs in biogenesis of WPBs.
source: Instead, our observations suggest functional redundancy of PKDs in biogenesis of WPBs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that all PKD members have similar effects on WPB biogenesis.

claim: A single knockdown of either PKD1 or PKD2 does not show any significant effect on WPB formation or secretion.
source: In fact, a single knockdown of either PKD1 or PKD2 does not show any significant effect on WPB formation as well as the secretion in earlier reports (Ketteler et al., 2017; Hao et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a statement about previous studies supported by citations.

claim: DAG is a conical-shaped lipid that is thought to be relatively concentrated in the TGN buds to increase membrane curvature.
source: DAG is a conical-shaped lipid that is thought to be relatively concentrated in the TGN buds to increase membrane curvature (Bankaitis et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a statement about DAG function supported by a citation.

claim: A theoretical model suggests that the presence of DAG on buds can stabilize the structure and prevent membrane fission.
source: A theoretical model suggests that the presence of DAG on buds can stabilize the structure and prevent membrane fission (Shemesh et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a statement about a theoretical model supported by a citation.

claim: The disappearance of DAG in the post-budded WPBs may suggest a conversion of DAG into other lipids that destabilize the membrane structure to enable membrane fission.
source: The disappearance of DAG in the post-budded WPBs may suggest a conversion of DAG into other lipids that destabilize the membrane structure to enable membrane fission.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the role of DAG in membrane fission.

claim: PI4P and phosphatidic acid are shown to work as pH biosensors in cells.
source: PI4P and phosphatidic acid, a lipid generated from DAG through single-step metabolism, are shown to work as pH biosensors in cells; the pH-dependent interaction with particular proteins regulates cellular processes such as membrane biogenesis and intracellular trafficking (Shin et al., 2020; Young et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a statement about lipid function supported by citations.

claim: A V0a2 mutation has been reported to cause bleeding diathesis in humans.
source: A V0a2 mutation has recently been reported to cause bleeding diathesis in humans (Karacan et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a statement about a clinical finding supported by a citation.

claim: Plasma VWF activity is significantly impaired in patients with V0a2 mutation without any substantial loss of plasma VWF antigen level.
source: Plasma VWF activity is significantly impaired in patients without any substantial loss of plasma VWF antigen level, thus exhibiting a typical sign of von Willebrand disease, although no associating mutation was found in the VWF gene.
evidence: This is a statement about a clinical finding.
